hints: Focus on selectivity here, you need a test that is positive for the alcohol but stays silent for both alkanes and alkenes.
Remember that sodium metal reacts with the O-H group in alcohols to give bubbles of hydrogen gas, but it does not react with C-C or C=C bonds.
Check the other three reagents against the alkene present, and ask yourself which ones would also be decolourised or give a positive result with C=C.
walkthrough:
**Define what a good test needs**

We have a mixture that is mostly alkanes and alkenes, with a little alcohol hidden in it. A good detecting reagent must react visibly with the alcohol only.

Think: positive for $\text{R-OH}$, negative for alkanes and alkenes.

**Test sodium with each functional group**

Sodium is a reactive metal that will remove the acidic H from an alcohol O-H group and fizz, giving hydrogen gas.

$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_{2}$$

**Confirm sodium ignores alkanes and alkenes**

Alkanes have only C-H and C-C bonds, and alkenes have C=C, neither is acidic enough to react with $\text{Na}$. So no bubbles means no alcohol, bubbles means alcohol is present. This makes it selective.

**Reject the non-selective reagents**

$\text{Br}_{2}$ in $\text{CCl}_{4}$ is decolourised by alkenes, and acidified $\text{KMnO}_{4}(\text{aq})$ is decolourised by both alkenes and alcohols, so both would already give a positive result because of the large amount of alkene. 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine only tests for carbonyls ($\text{C=O}$), so it stays negative for all three.

options.A: Sodium reacts only with the alcohol to give effervescence of H2 gas. It does not react with alkanes or alkenes, so any fizz proves alcohol is present in the mixture.
options.B: Br2 in CCl4 is decolourised from orange to colourless by electrophilic addition across the C=C of the alkene. Since the mixture is mainly alkenes, it will always give a positive result and cannot show whether alcohol is also present.
options.C: Aqueous KMnO4 is a strong oxidising agent decolourised from purple to colourless/brown by both alkenes and by many alcohols. It will react with the large amount of alkene present, so it is not selective for alcohol.
options.D: 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine gives an orange precipitate only with aldehydes and ketones containing C=O. It does not react with alcohols, alkanes or alkenes, so it would stay negative even if alcohol is present.
